speech act

if-clause

Context
Context is one of the aspects of the study of pragmatics.
______ is used traditionally to separate the premises from the conclusion.
horizontal line

______ are the effects of the utterance on the listener.
Perlocutionary acts
Perlocutionary acts are the effects of the utterance on the listener.

pronominal
Pronominals A pronominal (expression) is a non-anaphoric pronoun like he, she, him, her, his, etc. which must not refer to any higher expression within the clause immediately containing it.
______ is a sentence supplemented by information about the reference of any indexical expressions it contains.
proposition
A proposition is a sentence supplemented by information about the reference of any indexical expressions it contains.

______ is a type of utterance characterized by two distinctive features:  It is not truth-evaluable (i.e. it is neither true nor false).  Its uttering performs an action rather than simply describing one.
performative

A performative is a type of utterance characterized by two distinctive features:  It is not truth-evaluable (i.e. it is neither true nor false).  Its uttering performs an action rather than simply describing one.
______ refers to the world outside a text.
Deixis
Deixis refers to the world outside a text.
______ is an expression to which a pronoun refers and which normally precedes the pronoun in the text.
antecedent
An antecedent is an expression to which a pronoun refers and which normally precedes the pronoun in the text.
______ is a systematic way of explaining language use in context.
Pragmatics
Pragmatics is a systematic way of explaining language use in context.
______ are a class of pronouns beginning with the form of personal pronouns and ending with -self/-selves.
Reflexive pronouns
Reflexive pronouns are a class of pronouns beginning with the form of personal pronouns and ending with -self/-selves.
______ is a way of not saying exactly what you mean and expecting the addressee or your listener to guess or infer the meaning of your statement.
indirect speech acts
An indirect speech acts is a way of not saying exactly what you mean and expecting the addressee or your listener to guess or infer the meaning of your statement.
______ are the real actions which are performed by the utterance, where saying equals doing, as in betting, plighting one's troth, welcoming and warning.
Illocutionary acts

______ is the literal meaning of an idea whereas pragmatics is the implied meaning of the given idea.
Semantics
Semantics is the literal meaning of an idea whereas pragmatics is the implied meaning of the given idea.
______ are the demonstratives this, that, these and those; the place adverbs here and there; and the time adverbs now and then.
Common deictic words in English

______ is an incomplete proposition, hence it is called an open proposition.
generalization
The generalization is an incomplete proposition, hence it is called an open proposition.

Steps a and b
